zh.principle:
**算法**：ZUC 祖冲之流密码（ZUC）。### 三层结构

ZUC 是 128 位密钥/IV 的面向字流密码，由 16 级 31 位 LFSR、比特重组和非线性函数 F 产生 32 位密钥字；初始化 32 拍不输出，工作阶段每拍输出一个字。LFSR 单元取值限制在 1…2^31−1；Bit Reorganization 从 LFSR 抽取 128 位组成 4 个 32 位字；F 用两个 32 位记忆单元 R1/R2、S 盒 S0/S1 和线性变换 L1/L2 产生输出。### 初始化与工作

密钥装入把 128 位 key/IV 扩展成 16 个 31 位状态；初始化阶段运行 32 拍，把 F 的输出反馈进 LFSR，不产生密钥流；工作阶段每拍产生一个 32 位字，同时更新 LFSR。### 长度与版本

ZUC-128 用于 LTE 的 128-EEA3/128-EIA3；ZUC-256 为 5G 提供 256 位密钥，IV 可达 184 位，初始化与 MAC 生成阶段与 ZUC-128 不同。
zh.why: ZUC 是中国自主设计并进入 3GPP LTE 的流密码，同时提供 128-EEA3 机密性和 128-EIA3 完整性保护。它是少数由中国团队设计、被国际移动通信标准采用的密码算法。流密码不需要分组填充，适合按帧、按比特流加密的无线链路；LFSR 加非线性 F 的结构在硬件上面积小、吞吐高，适合基带芯片。
zh.used: 用于 LTE/5G 空口加密和完整性保护；3GPP 128-EEA3/128-EIA3 以 ZUC 为核心，5G 的 256-NEA3/256-NIA3 使用 ZUC-256。也可用于其他需要 128/256 位密钥的流式加密场景。工程要点：每个密钥/IV 组合只能产生有限长度的密钥流；IV 必须唯一；MAC 要与加密上下文绑定；不要把 ZUC 直接当通用哈希或认证码，完整性算法要按 128-EIA3 的 MAC 流程实现。
zh.broken: ZUC 1.4 的初始化不是单射，2010–2011 年的差分分析可让不同 IV 产生相同密钥流，直接导致密钥恢复；这促成 ZUC 1.5/1.6 的修改。最终版 ZUC-128 没有公开的实用全轮攻击，但侧信道、IV 复用、密钥流长度超限仍是现实风险。
zh.history:
ZUC 由中国科学院数据与通信保护研究教育中心设计，2010 年 7 月公开 ZUC 1.4 供评估；2011 年 1 月修订为 1.5，6 月发布 1.6；2011 年 9 月被 3GPP 采纳为 LTE 的 128-EEA3/128-EIA3 核心。2012 年发布 GM/T 0001 系列，2016 年 10 月发布 GB/T 33133.1-2016，2017 年 5 月实施；2020 年进入 ISO/IEC 18033-4 Amendment 1。ZUC-256 在 2018 年提出，用于 5G 256 位套件。它的命名来自南北朝数学家祖冲之，标准文本把算法、机密性算法和完整性算法分成三个部分。

en.principle:
**Algorithm**: ZUC (ZUC 祖冲之流密码). ### Three layers

ZUC is a word-oriented stream cipher: a 128-bit key, a 128-bit IV and 32-bit keystream words. The top layer is a 16-stage LFSR of 31-bit cells restricted to 1…2^31−1; the middle Bit Reorganization extracts 128 bits into four 32-bit words; the bottom nonlinear function F uses two 32-bit memory cells R1/R2, S-boxes S0/S1 and linear transforms L1/L2. ### Initialization and working stages

Key loading expands the 128-bit key/IV into sixteen 31-bit states. Initialization runs 32 clocks and feeds F back into the LFSR without producing keystream; the working stage outputs one 32-bit word per clock while updating the LFSR. ### Length and versions

ZUC-128 powers LTE 128-EEA3/128-EIA3. ZUC-256 provides 256-bit keys for 5G, supports IVs up to 184 bits, and differs from ZUC-128 in initialization and MAC generation.
en.why:
ZUC is a stream cipher designed in China and adopted by 3GPP LTE, providing both 128-EEA3 confidentiality and 128-EIA3 integrity. It is one of the few Chinese-designed algorithms adopted by an international mobile standard.

Stream ciphers need no block padding and fit frame- or bit-oriented wireless links; the LFSR plus nonlinear F structure has a small hardware footprint and high throughput, which suits baseband chips.
en.used:
It protects LTE/5G air-interface confidentiality and integrity: 3GPP 128-EEA3/128-EIA3 are built on ZUC, and 5G 256-NEA3/256-NIA3 use ZUC-256. It can also serve other streaming settings that need 128/256-bit keys.

Requirements: one key/IV pair may generate only a bounded keystream; IVs must be unique; the MAC must be bound to the encryption context; do not use ZUC as a general hash or MAC—follow the 128-EIA3 MAC flow.

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken:
ZUC 1.4’s initialization was not injective: differential analysis in 2010–2011 could make different IVs produce identical keystreams and recover keys, which led to ZUC 1.5/1.6. Final ZUC-128 has no publicly practical full-round attack, but side channels, IV reuse and over-long keystreams remain real risks.

Boundaries: ZUC supplies only a keystream, not authentication; pair it with 128-EIA3 or an AEAD construction. ZUC-256 uses different parameters and IV lengths, so a 128-bit implementation cannot be reused unchanged.
en.history:
ZUC was designed by the Chinese Academy of Sciences’ Data Assurance and Communication Security Research Center. ZUC 1.4 was published for evaluation in July 2010; 1.5 followed in January 2011 and 1.6 in June 2011; 3GPP adopted it for LTE 128-EEA3/128-EIA3 in September 2011. GM/T 0001 appeared in 2012, GB/T 33133.1-2016 was published in October 2016 and took effect in May 2017, and ISO/IEC 18033-4 Amendment 1 added ZUC in 2020. ZUC-256 was proposed in 2018 for 5G 256-bit suites.

Its name honors the Northern and Southern Dynasties mathematician Zu Chongzhi; the standard splits the algorithm, confidentiality algorithm and integrity algorithm into three parts.
